items.stem: How is the recoverable amount of an asset defined under IAS 36?

options.text: The higher of its fair value less costs of disposal and its value in use
options.rationale: Correct: recoverable amount is the higher of the two measures.

options.text: The lower of its fair value less costs of disposal and its value in use
options.rationale: It is the higher, not the lower, of the two.

options.text: Its original cost less accumulated depreciation
options.rationale: That is carrying amount, not recoverable amount.
Insured value is not the measure of recoverable amount.

items.explanation: Correct: recoverable amount is the higher of the two measures.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about impairment losses under IAS 36 are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Goodwill is tested for impairment at least annually, irrespective of indicators
options.rationale: Correct: goodwill (and certain intangibles) must be tested at least annually.

options.text: An impairment loss on goodwill is not reversed in a later period
options.rationale: Correct: goodwill impairment losses are never reversed.

options.text: Impairment losses may only ever be recognised at disposal
options.rationale: Impairment is recognised when recoverable amount is below carrying amount, not only at disposal.

options.text: An impairment loss on a machine can never be reversed
options.rationale: Non-goodwill impairment losses can be reversed if recoverable amount recovers.

items.explanation: Correct: goodwill (and certain intangibles) must be tested at least annually.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: An entity recognised an impairment loss on goodwill two years ago. The cash-generating unit's performance has since recovered strongly. May the goodwill impairment be reversed?

options.text: No; an impairment loss recognised on goodwill is never reversed
options.rationale: Correct: goodwill impairment losses are not reversed under any circumstances.

options.text: Yes, in full, because the unit has recovered
Yes, but only up to half the original loss
options.rationale: No partial reversal of goodwill impairment is permitted.
Director approval does not permit a goodwill reversal.

items.explanation: Correct: goodwill impairment losses are not reversed under any circumstances.
